author: Peach Tree Times
title: Army veteran Bob Crecco revisits Omaha Beach during Normandy legacy flight
text:
Army veteran Bob Crecco returned to Omaha Beach on June 10, retracing the steps of his landing there during World War II. The visit was part of a program that allows veterans to revisit significant locations from their wartime experiences.
Local World War II historian and tour guide Florent Plana assisted Crecco in identifying the precise spot where his landing craft came ashore on June 7, 1944. Plana also pointed out the site, four miles away, where Crecco’s division had originally been scheduled to arrive. During the visit, a French family now residing on the land welcomed Crecco into their home for coffee as Plana shared maps detailing his movements from that day.
Later in the day, Crecco visited the 2nd Infantry Division Monument on Omaha Beach. There he paused to honor fallen comrades before reflecting with team members over breakfast about his experience. “I was very glad to get to return,” he said.
Delta Air Lines supports such programs by providing global air travel through an extensive network connecting more than 350 destinations worldwide and utilizing a fleet comprising various aircraft models from manufacturers such as Airbus and Boeing, according to the official website.
Delta Air Lines operates as a publicly traded entity incorporated in Delaware under U.S. law and delivers scheduled transport for passengers and cargo across domestic and international sites, according to the official website.
